item.title: backlog list has no --ready filter — users cannot quickly see sprint candidates
item.intent: Users must be able to run 'backlog list --ready' and see only items that pass readiness gates, so they can decide what to run next without scanning the full table.
item.description: cmd_backlog_list() supports --status, --type, and --priority filters but has no --ready flag. Users preparing for a sprint must scan the full READY column to find actionable items. A --ready flag would filter the output to only items where readyForSprint is true, consistent with the existing filter pattern. The complementary --no-ready flag (items where readyForSprint is false) is useful for grooming triage.
steps: In cmd_backlog_list(), add local ready_filter='' before the flag loop; add --ready case setting ready_filter=true and --no-ready setting ready_filter=false
After the existing --status and --type filter conditions, add ready_filter to the jq select expression: if ready_filter is set, add 'and (.readyForSprint == (env.READY_FILTER == "true"))' using --arg
Pass the ready_filter value as a jq --arg or env var into the jq pipeline
Add --ready and --no-ready to the usage message and cmd_help output
Run shellcheck — confirm zero new warnings
acceptanceCriteria: aishore backlog list --ready shows only items where readyForSprint is true
aishore backlog list --no-ready shows only items where readyForSprint is false
aishore backlog list with no ready filter still shows all items (backwards compatible)
